title: Singleton Fourier energy of a sign-valued function
statement: Let $n\ge 0$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$. With Fourier–Walsh coefficients defined using the uniform measure on the Boolean cube, the singleton coefficients satisfy $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\widehat f(\{i\})^2\le1$.
hypotheses_covered: The dimension $n$ is a natural number
$f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. Every $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat f(\{i\})^2\le1$.
